scope.description: A focused direction drawn from Schiele's radical works on paper around 1910–1914. An emphatic, angular contour carries the subject's structure and tension; asymmetrical open ground balances the silhouette, while dry, sparse color remains attached to selected forms. This is a study of line, figure-ground pressure, and material restraint, not a prescribed body or narrative.
limitations: Preserve the requested subject, identity, pose, clothing, and body type; do not default to nudity, self-portraiture, erotic framing, or a contorted pose.
Apply angular stylization only as far as the subject remains recognizable and the requested action stays legible.
Keep paper ground and sparse color subordinate to the requested medium and color constraints; do not impose a fixed palette on every image.

rules.applies_when: The requested image is a drawing or watercolor study with a clearly defined subject.
rules.instruction: Vary the contour's pressure, direction, and continuity to stress the requested subject's structure; allow purposeful angular breaks, but retain enough anatomical or object landmarks to preserve identity and action.
rules.observable: The line feels deliberate and structurally expressive, with a few stronger turns or interruptions carrying more weight than secondary edges.
rules.reject_when: Every edge has the same weight, the contour becomes decorative calligraphy, or angularity distorts a user-specified identity or action.
rules.avoid: uniform outlines, ornamental flourishes, and arbitrary anatomical distortion

rules.applies_when: The composition includes a distinct subject against visible paper or a quiet field.
rules.instruction: Place the subject asymmetrically and let open ground press against or interrupt selected parts of its silhouette; keep the negative shapes intentional and protect the requested focal landmarks.
rules.observable: The occupied and unoccupied areas create a taut, readable balance rather than a centered cutout or evenly filled page.
rules.reject_when: Empty ground is merely leftover margin, the silhouette closes into a generic sticker shape, or open areas erase critical parts of the subject.
rules.avoid: centered badge layouts, uniform page filling, and accidental blank gaps

rules.applies_when: The user requests watercolor, gouache, or another paper-based painted study.
rules.instruction: Use a few restrained, dry color passages on selected forms and leave paper visible between them; assign colors locally to the requested subject and avoid spreading one hue as an all-over wash.
rules.observable: Color supports the form in separate, economical accents while the paper remains an active part of the surface.
rules.reject_when: Color becomes a uniform filter, wet atmospheric blending replaces line and paper, or the user's palette request is ignored.
rules.avoid: global sepia, generalized watercolor haze, and full-page opaque fill

joint_checks.instruction: Let contour, open ground, and sparse color reinforce the same structural emphasis without forcing a recurring subject, pose, or palette.
joint_checks.observable: The subject remains recognizable, the line carries expressive weight, and open paper and localized color complete rather than decorate the composition.
